emails.subject: Larkmoor's Series B and two new centers
emails.body:
Hi there,

I saw Larkmoor closed a $28 million Series B in May to add two fulfillment centers. New sites mean new shift schedules, usually built while the existing centers are busy.

Example Shift Software builds warehouse shift schedules from forecast order volume, for every site in one place.

Who owns scheduling for the new centers?

[Your name], Example Shift Software

If this isn't relevant, reply "no" and I won't follow up.
emails.fact: Series B $28M, 2026-05-19, to add two fulfillment centers (news-wire.example)

emails.subject: Re: Larkmoor's Series B and two new centers
emails.body:
Hi there,

In e-commerce fulfillment, order volume can swing hour to hour. Teams use our app to match staff to demand per hour, which cuts overtime, and floor staff swap or pick up shifts on their phones instead of calling the office.

How do your four centers build next week's schedule today?

[Your name], Example Shift Software

Reply "no" to stop these emails.
emails.fact: e-commerce fulfillment from four fulfillment centers (larkmoor-fulfillment.example homepage)

emails.subject: Close the loop?
emails.body:
Hi there,

I don't want to crowd your inbox. If scheduling for the new centers isn't a priority this quarter, no problem; I'll close this out.

If it is, 20 minutes is enough to build a sample week from your own volumes. Should I close the loop, or is that worth a look?

[Your name], Example Shift Software

Reply "no" to stop these emails.

problems_worth_testing.hypothesis: Peak-season shifts are planned from last year's roster, not from forecast order volume
problems_worth_testing.your_problem: build shift schedules from forecast order volume

problems_worth_testing.your_problem: cut overtime by matching staff to demand per hour
problems_worth_testing.rules_it_out: Overtime stays flat in peak, or is a deliberate choice.

problems_worth_testing.hypothesis: Each of the sites keeps its own schedule, so the new VP cannot see one view
problems_worth_testing.rules_it_out: One system already holds every site's schedule.

discovery_questions.q: You now list 6 sites, including the new Columbus East page. How is a week's schedule built at each one today?
When the Indianapolis site opened, how were its first schedules set up?
Your ads this month push peak-season capacity. What changes in staffing when that capacity fills?
You are hiring for warehouse operations roles in Columbus. Which of those hires is meant to fix a scheduling problem, if any?
What did overtime look like last peak, and who owns that number?
With a new VP of Warehouse Operations in October, what is on the first 90 days list?
If you changed how shifts are planned, who besides operations would need to agree, and by when?
